prompt: ripgrep NUL bytes handling without text flag
answer:
Without `-a/--text`, ripgrep uses NUL-byte-based binary detection:

- A file containing a NUL byte is considered binary.
- By default, ripgrep stops searching the file when it encounters the NUL byte.
- If the NUL occurs after a match, ripgrep may suppress that match, stop searching, and emit a warning.
- `--binary` makes ripgrep continue past NUL bytes until it finds a match or reaches EOF, then warns if it stops after a match.
- `-a/--text` disables special NUL/binary handling and searches the file as text, potentially printing binary data.

Sources: [Debian `rg` manpage](https://manpages.debian.org/testing/ripgrep/rg.1.en.html), [ripgrep GUIDE](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/blob/master/GUIDE.md).
